courses.title: Choose what you will build.
courses.lead: Design a chip, build a smart device, program a robot or train an AI model. In every four-year B.Tech, you build a working project each semester.

sections.title: Four ways to build AI systems

items.title: Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology)
items.text: Design the chips inside phones, cars and AI systems. A good fit if you enjoy logic, puzzles and precise work. Explore careers in chip design, verification and physical design.

items.title: Electronics and Computer Engineering
items.text: Put circuits, software and AI together in smart devices such as EV chargers and medical monitors. A good fit if both electronics and computing interest you. Explore careers in embedded systems, firmware and product engineering.

items.title: Robotics and Artificial Intelligence
items.text: Build robots and drones that sense and move. A good fit if you want your code to move things in the real world. Explore careers in robotics, automation and machine perception.

items.title: CSE (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning)
items.text: Train models on data, test their predictions and put them to work in software. A good fit if you enjoy mathematics, programming and analysing data.

sections.title: Bring a product to market
sections.intro: Learn how to finance a product, source its parts, reach customers and grow a business. Work alongside future engineers and use AI as a business tool.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The four B.Tech programmes share a project-based learning model. Projects increase in difficulty and lead to a final semester of supervised engineering work. Individual practical assessments record the skills each student can demonstrate independently.

courses/electronics-computer-engineering.title: Build the whole smart device.
courses/electronics-computer-engineering.lead: Design a circuit board, write its firmware and run AI on the device. Take a working prototype through a pilot batch and a field trial.

sections.title: How a smart device works
body: A smartwatch, an EV charger and a heart monitor each depend on circuits and software working together. This course follows the work across that boundary, from a sensor reading to a device someone can use.

sections.title: From calibrated instrument to field trial

items.title: Semester 1 · A smart measuring instrument
items.text: Design and calibrate your own instrument.

items.title: Semester 2 · A connected device with a custom circuit board
items.text: Build a working device on a circuit board you designed.

items.title: Semester 3 · An embedded board
items.text: Make your own board process a real-world signal.

items.title: Semester 4 · Real-time motor control
items.text: Build a controller that balances, steers or drives a motor.

items.title: Semester 5 · On-device AI on Linux
items.text: Build a Linux-based product that runs a model on the device itself.

items.title: Semester 6 · A 10-unit pilot batch
items.text: Build a secure product and make a pilot batch of 10 units.

items.title: Semester 7 · A smart device in field trials
items.text: Take a complete smart device from a user's problem to a field trial.

items.title: Semester 8 · 16–20 weeks of engineering work
items.text: Put your skills to work in a company or the Product Studio.

sections.title: Circuits, firmware and edge AI

items.title: Hardware
items.text: Circuit and PCB design, ARM and RISC-V microcontrollers, FPGA, and design for manufacturing.

items.title: Software
items.text: C, C++ and Python, real-time operating systems, embedded Linux, device drivers and device security.

items.title: Embedded intelligence
items.text: Signal processing, control, machine learning and edge AI.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in embedded systems and firmware, edge AI, embedded Linux, IoT products, and automotive and EV electronics. The skills also support building a hardware startup.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The sequence starts with measurement and circuit design, then introduces embedded computing and real-time control. Later builds bring together on-device machine learning, device security, pilot manufacturing and a field trial. Individual practical assessments document what each student can do independently.

links.label: See how projects and skill tests work

faq.question: What does Electronics and Computer Engineering cover?
faq.answer: It combines electronics and computer engineering in one degree. You design the hardware, write the software and learn how the two work together.

faq.question: Can I take a software job?
faq.answer: Yes. The curriculum includes programming, data structures, operating systems and software engineering.

courses/vlsi.eyebrow: B.Tech · Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology)
courses/vlsi.title: Design a chip from logic to layout.
courses/vlsi.lead: Test digital circuits on programmable hardware, design a processor core and take a chip from specification to physical layout.

sections.title: Inside a silicon chip
body: A single chip can contain billions of switches on a piece of silicon smaller than a fingernail. As India invests in semiconductor manufacturing, engineers are needed to turn specifications into circuits and show that those circuits work.

sections.title: From FPGA circuits to a chip layout
sections.intro: These projects illustrate the proposed year-by-year progression. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

items.title: Year 1 · Digital circuits
items.text: Build and test circuits on programmable hardware called FPGA boards.

items.title: Year 2 · A processor core
items.text: Design the part of a chip that fetches and executes instructions.

items.title: Year 3 · Verified designs
items.text: Verify digital designs and work on analog and mixed-signal circuits.

items.title: Year 4 · A complete chip design
items.text: Carry a design from specification to physical layout, then apply your skills in a supervised work semester.

sections.title: Circuit design, verification and layout
body: The proposed curriculum covers semiconductor devices, digital and analog circuit design, Verilog and SystemVerilog, computer architecture, design verification, physical design and industry design tools.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in RTL design, design verification, physical design, analog and mixed-signal design, and semiconductor validation.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The proposed sequence goes from the behaviour of individual circuits to designing a processor and checking a full chip layout. An FPGA lets you test a digital design on programmable hardware while it is still being developed.

faq.question: What does VLSI stand for?
faq.answer: Very-large-scale integration. It is the design of complex circuits that integrate large numbers of transistors onto a single chip.

faq.question: Can I see the final list of projects?
faq.answer: Ask admissions for the current curriculum and project brief for the campus you are considering.

courses/robotics-ai.title: Turn sensor data into controlled motion.
courses/robotics-ai.lead: Program a mobile robot to sense and steer, control a robotic arm and use computer vision in moving machines.

sections.title: How a robot acts on what it sees
body: Robots in warehouses, farms, hospitals and factories have to make decisions in a physical world. A camera gives a machine a view of its surroundings. Software interprets what it sees. Mechanics and control turn that decision into movement.

sections.title: Mobile robots, arms and vision systems
sections.intro: These projects illustrate the proposed year-by-year progression. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

items.title: Year 1 · Mobile robots
items.text: Build robots that detect their surroundings and steer.

items.title: Year 2 · Robotic arms
items.text: Build an arm and control how precisely it moves.

items.title: Year 3 · Machines that see
items.text: Work on computer vision, drones and self-driving platforms.

items.title: Year 4 · Robots that learn
items.text: Train robots using data and simulation, then apply your skills in a supervised work semester.

sections.title: Motion control, perception and simulation
body: The proposed curriculum covers programming and algorithms, mechanics and mechatronics, motors and control, embedded systems, kinematics and motion planning, computer vision, machine learning, ROS 2 and simulation.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in robotics, industrial automation, machine perception, autonomous systems and drone technology. The course also offers a foundation for building a robotics company.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The projects progressively combine sensor inputs, motion control and perception. Students use simulation to test behaviours and learn to evaluate those behaviours on a physical system. Individual practical assessments complement team builds.

links.label: See how projects and skill tests work

faq.question: How much of the course involves coding?
faq.answer: Programming and algorithms are core skills. You also write software for sensors, controllers, motion planning and machine vision.

faq.question: Do I need robotics experience to start?
faq.answer: The learning model starts with foundational skills and smaller builds. More complex projects follow as you practise programming, electronics and control.

courses/cse-ai-ml.eyebrow: B.Tech · CSE (Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning)
courses/cse-ai-ml.title: Train, test and deploy AI models.
courses/cse-ai-ml.lead: Work with data, train models and test their predictions. Turn those models into recommendation, vision and language applications.

sections.title: What makes a model reliable
body: A model learns patterns from the data you give it. You need statistics, sound data and a way to test predictions on examples the model has never seen. That is how you find where a model works, where it fails and what to improve.

sections.title: From datasets to deployed software
sections.intro: These projects illustrate the proposed year-by-year progression. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

items.title: Year 1 · Programs and data analysis
items.text: Write software and analyse data to solve practical problems.

items.title: Year 2 · A recommendation model
items.text: Build a model such as a recommendation engine and test its results.

items.title: Year 3 · Vision and language applications
items.text: Build applications using computer vision, language models and generative AI.

items.title: Year 4 · An AI product for real users
items.text: Take a product to real users, then apply your skills in a supervised work semester.

sections.title: Machine learning, data engineering and deployment
body: The proposed curriculum covers Python, data structures, algorithms, mathematics for machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, language models, generative AI, data engineering, model deployment and monitoring, and responsible AI.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work as an AI or machine learning engineer, data scientist, applied AI engineer or MLOps engineer. The skills also support building an AI startup.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The course design moves from programming and data to training, evaluation and deployment. MLOps is the engineering work of putting models into use, monitoring how they perform and maintaining them over time.

links.label: See how AI is used in projects and assessments

faq.question: If AI writes code, why study computer science?
faq.answer: Computer science teaches you to design systems, evaluate the software a tool generates and improve the models that generate it.

faq.question: Will I learn to deploy a model?
faq.answer: The proposed curriculum includes model deployment and monitoring alongside training and evaluation.

courses/management.title: Take a product from lab to market.
courses/management.lead: Work with engineers to find customers, set prices and plan how a product is sourced, made and sold. Use data and AI to inform those decisions.

sections.title: What it takes to bring a product to market
body: A prototype needs a supply chain, customers and a business behind it to reach the market. Engineers and managers work together to make those pieces fit. This programme teaches you to make business decisions with a practical understanding of the product.

sections.title: Two degrees, four specialisations
sections.intro: The proposed BBA format is three or four years and the proposed MBA format is two years. Ask admissions about the duration and options at your campus.

items.title: AI for Business
items.text: Use data and AI tools to make decisions, automate work and improve how an organisation runs.

items.title: Supply Chain and Operations Management
items.text: Learn how to source, make and move products across India and the world.

items.title: AI for Marketing and Sales
items.text: Find customers, build brands and grow revenue with AI tools for marketing and sales.

items.title: Entrepreneurship and New Ventures
items.text: Take an idea toward a company by finding customers, setting prices, exploring funding and planning for growth.

sections.title: From first customer to factory order
body: Management students can join engineering teams and work on bringing a product to market, from identifying the first customer to preparing for a factory order. Company projects connect coursework to decisions and constraints that businesses face.

sections.title: Where it leads
body: Explore work in business analysis, operations and supply chain, marketing and sales, or start a company of your own.

sections.title: For those who want the detail
body: The management programme pairs business fundamentals with company projects and product work. Cross-disciplinary teams use cost, customer and operations evidence to make decisions about how a product reaches the market.

faq.question: Which degree should I explore?
faq.answer: The BBA is an undergraduate business degree. The MBA is a postgraduate business degree. Ask admissions which entry routes apply to you.

faq.question: Can BBA and MBA students choose the same specialisations?
faq.answer: The programme proposes the same four specialisations for both degrees. Confirm availability for your preferred campus with admissions.
